image_description: A group of sea lions in a pool with turquoise water. One sea lion is swimming upright in the center background, showing its head and neck. Another sea lion is visible on the right side, mostly submerged with only its head and upper back showing. On the left, several sea lions are resting on rocks at the edge of the pool. The background shows a concrete enclosure wall and some vegetation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible heads are relatively smooth; no prominent sagittal crest is clearly visible on any individual, likely due to distance, angle, or they being females/juveniles.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small but distinct external ear flaps are visible on the heads of the sea lions, particularly the one in the center and the one on the right, confirming they are otariids (sea lions) and not phocids (true seals).
